newsitem.title: INDIA: Non-Aligned unite to condemn U.S. embargo on Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Non-Aligned unite to condemn U.S. embargo on Cuba.

text.p: Cuba's foreign minister said on Tuesday the world's non-aligned nations had unanimously condemned the long-standing U.S. embargo against the communist island.

Citing recent U.S. opposition to Cuban exports of pyjamas to Canada, Foreign Minister Roberto Robaina Gonzalez said Washington's attempts to compel other nations to join its efforts to isolate Cuba had reached ridiculous proportions.
"This is a laughable example of Senators from a powerful country spending sleepless nights over Cuban pyjamas," Robaina told a business meeting in New Delhi.
Robaina told Reuters the issue of U.S. trade sanctions against Cuba was discussed by the two-day conference of the 113-member Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) which ended in New Delhi on Tuesday.
"There was a unanimous condemnation of the embargo. We didn't have to press any NAM member to do that," Robaina said.
The battle over sales in Canada of Cuban pyjamas occurred against a broader background of Canadian, European and Mexican anger at a year-old U.S. measure known as the Helms-Burton law.

That act, signed into law by U.S. President Bill Clinton after Cuban MiG fighters shot down two small private U.S. planes off Cuba in February 1996, seeks to compel other nations to join U.S. efforts to isolate Cuba.
The Canadian unit of U.S. Wal-Mart Stores Inc. has been locked in a controversy with Ottawa after withdrawing Cuban pyjamas from its outlets.
The Canadian government has pressured Wal-Mart Canada into putting the cotton pyjamas back on store shelves.
This has placed the retailer in potential breach of U.S. laws.
"We are continuing to invite foreign investments and trade with greater zeal," Robaina said. "So that when the blockade is lifted, there is less space for the United States."
